Evening newswrap: 6 killed in U'khand chopper crash; global LNG prices jump 6% & more
Dolly Parton's free book programme sees 950 new sign-ups and $150,000 in donations after her death
stories.summary: In the wake of Dolly Parton's passing, the Imagination Library saw a remarkable increase in registrations. In August alone, Knox County welcomed nearly 950 new children to the program. Additionally, over $150,000 was generated through a fundraising initiative to bolster the library's mission. Established in 1995, this program ensures that young readers receive free books every month until the age of five, proudly distributing over four million books to date.

stories.title: Paid to hire, paid to work: Inside India’s Rs 99,446 cr plan to reshape the formal workforce
stories.summary: Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) is introduced to enhance formal employment across various sectors. The scheme includes financial incentives for both employers and first-time employees entering the formal job market. PMVBRY aims to create more than 3.5 crore jobs including 1.92 crore first-time workers by 2027. It targets an increase in manufacturing employment with unique incentives for the sector.

stories.title: Form 7 row: Supreme Court directs EC to probe bulk applications during Uttar Pradesh SIR
Lost Renaissance plaques found in English home sell for £100,000 after 142 years
stories.summary: A pair of exquisite 16th-century maiolica plaques by renowned artist Francesco Xanto Avelli recently fetched an impressive £100,000 at auction after lying unnoticed in a Dorset home for years. The family unearthed these extraordinary pieces while seeking expert advice, discovering they were part of a significant series illustrating the tale of Cyrus the Great. This auction underscores the remarkable rarity and cultural value of these Italian Renaissance treasures.

stories.title: Quebec home built from 200,000 recycled bottles, assembled in just three days
stories.summary: In a remarkable development, a two-bedroom house located in Saint-Rémi-d'Amherst, Quebec, has been built using an innovative construction method known as PakVert. This technique employs panels crafted from recycled plastic bottles, resulting in a building process that took merely three days. By minimizing construction waste and cutting costs by approximately 35 percent, this initiative contributes significantly to affordable housing and environmental sustainability in Canada.

stories.title: Boston Celtics owners donate $200 million to children's hospital
Husband’s home valuation rejected in Tennessee divorce appeal
stories.summary: In a contentious marital dispute, a Tennessee appeals court confirmed the trial court's assessment of a marital home valued at $160,400, awarding the wife 75% of the home's equity—approximately $47,139. The husband's higher valuation based on comparable sales was dismissed by the court. Moreover, the court invalidated the husband's artwork and tool valuations, mandating their reassessment. It also made essential amendments to the permanent parenting plan concerning visitation rights.

stories.title: Indiana University’s free AI course attracts over 114,000 learners
Arkansas took just 1.62 acres from a family trust and valued the loss at $417,825; after an 11-year fight over road access, court upholds $3 million award
stories.summary: A long-standing legal dispute in Arkansas involved a land acquisition that significantly impacted property access. The Arkansas Court of Appeals recently upheld a $3 million jury compensation award related to this case. The case emerged after the Arkansas State Highway Commission's project restricted access to a property owned by the William Major Lewis Trust. Evidence submitted demonstrated that the remaining property value was adversely affected by the highway work.

stories.title: Georgia couple won $37 million after their 3-year-old son died during cancer treatment; judge cut it to $2 million, appeals court raises award to $3 million
stories.summary: A couple in Georgia has triumphed in their legal battle, securing a $3 million judgment after an appeals court re-evaluated their son's death case. This decision overturned a previous reduction of a $37 million jury award to just $2 million. Their son, who succumbed to stage-four Burkitt lymphoma, faced complications during his treatment. The court recognized the parents as distinct entities under state law, enabling them to seek higher restitution.

stories.title: 'Want to sow confusion': BJP targets Rahul Gandhi ahead of INDIA bloc's 'Delhi Chalo' march
'They plotted': Ex-Manipur CM Biren Singh blames BJP leaders for ouster, questions continued violence
Uttarakhand chopper crash: All six people on board chopper that crashed in Joshimath have died - what we know so far
stories.summary: A helicopter operated by Trans Bharat Aviation crashed near Joshimath, resulting in the death of all six people on board. The aircraft lost contact during its flight from Badrinath to Dehradun on Friday afternoon. Search and rescue teams were deployed to locate the crash site amid adverse weather conditions, including heavy rain and snowfall.

stories.title: 'I will be present in court': Anant Singh to surrender by Dec 1 after SC cancels bail; accuses Neeraj Kumar of plotting case
Five compulsory board papers, optional skill subject as safety net: CBSE clarifies Class X scheme
stories.summary: Current class IX batch can choose between school-assessed Kaushal Vikas and 22 board-examined skill subjects; clarification aimed at protecting students' interests

stories.title: 'BJP like Angad's foot': Amit Shah warns Akhilesh, says SP won't return to power in UP for 30 years
'No multiple protests, entire oppn together': Rahul Gandhi says INDIA bloc defending 'idea of India', people's votes
Uttarakhand: Chopper returning from Badrinath crashes near Joshimath; rescue op under way for 6 on board
Did Lacy misunderstand his Japan restaurant bill? Streamer reveals what actually happened
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Nick "Lacy" has addressed a mix-up involving a $12,000 restaurant bill he thought he owed in Japan. Initially confused due to language issues, he later discovered he was only responsible for extra food. Realizing the impact of his comments, Lacy has since apologized to the restaurant for inadvertently causing them negative publicity and acknowledged the necessity of clearer communication.

stories.title: Brittany and Patrick Mahomes’ Allergy-Friendly Restaurant Gets First Approval in Kansas City
stories.summary: Brittany Mahomes is spearheading a valuable initiative aimed at enhancing food allergy safety in restaurants throughout Kansas City with the 15 and FARE program. This initiative educates both eateries and locals on effective allergy management, with Joe's KC proudly becoming the first restaurant to earn this designation by implementing crucial safety practice improvements.

stories.title: 'A win is a win': Israel opposition leader Lapid reacts to Netanyahu's poll setback
stories.summary: Yair Lapid stated that the anti-Netanyahu bloc won the election while indicating the need for coalition talks. The bloc secured 67 seats in the Knesset, insufficient for a majority. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition obtained 53 seats, lacking a clear path to govern. Lapid emphasized the importance of patience during the ongoing discussions amidst uncertainty. He assured the public that negotiations are active, though results may not be immediately visible.

stories.title: 'Will serve until my last breath': PM Modi declares in Gujarat - top quotes
Scientists discover silk traces on 101 ancient objects in China, uncover clues to ancient rituals
stories.summary: Scientists studying 3,000-year-old objects from China's Sanxingdui archaeological site have found silk traces on 101 artefacts, including bronze masks, gold, jade and ivory objects. Published in the journal Antiquity, the study suggests that ancient Shu people used silk to wrap or cover objects during rituals. Researchers also identified red pigments and different weaving patterns, offering clues about ancient textile practices.

stories.title: INDIA bloc postpones 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar due to rains
'Modi nahi jayenge' slogan raised at PM's Gujarat event; Congress retorts, 'you wish!'
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre in Gujarat on Friday, unveiling development projects totaling over Rs 14,000 crore. He also released the latest PM-KISAN installment, benefiting farmers with Rs 19,000 crore. The trip included plans to enhance Ahmedabad's metro network and state roads, while also announcing new initiatives for the dairy and childcare sectors.

stories.title: Appeals court revives lawsuit over eyewear retailer sharing customer data with Meta
Australia’s stingless bees may help fight antibiotic resistance
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Sydney are investigating the medicinal properties of honey from stingless bees. The honey has shown effectiveness against various bacterial and fungal pathogens, including difficult-to-treat strains. Findings suggest that sugarbag honey is comparable in strength to well-known medical-grade honeys. While propolis displayed selective antimicrobial activity, the reason for honey's potency remains unclear. Further research is needed to identify the beneficial compounds within the honey.

stories.title: Arkansas couple pays $8,000 for access to landlocked property, loses court battle with neighbours
stories.summary: An Arkansas couple who paid their neighbours $8,000 for an 18-foot-wide road to access their land near Beaver Lake have lost a dispute over its location. The Arkansas Court of Appeals upheld a route along the neighbours' property boundary, despite concerns about construction costs and difficult terrain. One judge disagreed, warning that the approved route could be unusable without expensive work.

stories.title: German teacher on sick leave for 16 years, collected nearly €1 million in salary; now faces fraud charges over €248,000
stories.summary: A 62-year-old German educator faces fraud charges after reportedly taking a 16-year sick leave, during which she allegedly collected over €248,000 in salary. Investigators believe she fabricated medical documentation to support her prolonged absence from the classroom. Although she engaged in scuba diving, there’s no evidence of her undertaking any other professional work. The court is currently reviewing the case to determine if a full trial is warranted.

stories.title: Israel election results: Neither Netanyahu nor oppn wins majority; what happens next?
stories.summary: Israel faces a political deadlock after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc fell short of the 61 seats needed for a majority. With Arab-led parties holding 19 seats, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot could seek their support to form a government. However, ideological differences complicate the numbers. A unity government, opposition defections or another election are among four possible scenarios, according to CNN.

stories.title: Night polo goesmainstream in Jaipur
University of Georgia secures $8 million NOAA grant to plan restoration of acres of salt marsh
stories.summary: University of Georgia has received an $8 million grant to restore salt marsh habitat across four coastal states. The initiative, which spans from North Carolina to Florida, will assess the use of dredged sediment. This project aims to elevate marshes and support diverse wildlife while addressing rising sea levels and pollution. Proposed restoration sites include Bird-Long Island, Cape Lookout National Seashore, Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge, and Julia’s Island.

stories.title: Surrender before December 1: Supreme Court cancels bail of expelled JD(U) leader Anant Singh in Dularchand Yadav murder case
An Ohio appeals court on Oct 26 upheld a zoning ban on Airbnb rentals in a 140-home neighbourhood
stories.summary: An Ohio appellate court has confirmed a zoning restriction prohibiting short-term rentals in a suburban area. Michael A. Clevenger, an owner looking to operate an Airbnb, faced opposition from neighbors concerned about excessive noise, parking congestion, and heightened safety risks from frequent guests. This ruling emphasizes the importance of adhering to local zoning regulations that maintain the integrity of residential neighborhoods, reinforcing existing legal frameworks against short-term rental operations.

stories.title: A $295 million Malibu mansion by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Tadao Ando was quietly on the market when Kanye West came unannounced
stories.summary: Kanye West made an unplanned visit to a stunning Malibu mansion crafted by Tadao Ando, spending four days there. He secured a stay without prior arrangement, likening his presence to that of Elvis Presley. Meanwhile, the estate was later sold to Jay-Z and Beyoncé, breaking sales records. West's personal Ando-designed property, however, is grappling with legal and financial troubles, leaving its future uncertain due to ongoing foreclosure issues.

stories.title: Maine Forest Protections Secure Jobs: Coalition preserves 27,000 acres; working forest still supports timber, recreation
stories.summary: In a remarkable achievement, over 27,000 acres of forestland in western Maine have been safeguarded through collaborative conservation efforts. This extensive initiative spanned six years, bringing together environmental groups, state agencies, and local trusts. Preserving this land is vital for ensuring clean drinking water for more than 200,000 residents while supporting timber jobs and enhancing recreational opportunities and habitats for wildlife in the area.

stories.title: Margo Fairchild built a 240-square-foot home by hand and caught HGTV’s attention

'Everyone understands who will suffer consequences': Congress's Imran Masood on Owaisi's INDIA bloc alliance offer
India calls for protecting freedom of navigation, global trade at UN amid maritime security threats
stories.summary: India strongly condemned the attacks against commercial vessels and highlighted the importance of maritime security at the UN. Harish Parvathaneni stressed the impact of disruptions at critical maritime choke points on global supply chains. He noted the potential of emerging technologies like AI to enhance maritime security while also posing new risks. The representative emphasized the need for safeguards and clear responsibility regarding technological deployment.

stories.title: Once a textile giant, now homes and offices: Virginia’s abandoned mill gets a $110 million makeover
stories.summary: Dan River Falls embodies a transformative redevelopment of the historic White Mill, originally constructed in 1920, located in Danville. Completed in November 2024, the first phase features 190 residential apartments. Plans for the future include developing a vibrant riverfront park and retail area. This public-private collaboration strives to maintain the mill's historic integrity while breathing new life into the community and catering to workforce housing needs.

stories.title: Cleopatra’s eye makeup secret? Ancient Egyptians used lead-based kohl
stories.summary: In ancient Egypt, kohl was more than just a cosmetic; it served dual purposes, enhancing beauty while protecting the eyes. Studies indicate that its ingredients could boost immune responses, making it a valuable tool for health. Both men and women embraced the use of black and green powders, and ancient texts highlight the fusion of cosmetics with medicine, revealing the intricate beliefs surrounding beauty and wellness in that era.

stories.title: Common daily fiber supplement was found to significantly reduce knee pain and improve strength
stories.summary: A recent study from the University of Nottingham unveils exciting findings regarding inulin supplementation for knee osteoarthritis. Participants not only experienced a reduction in joint pain, but they also enhanced their grip strength and sensitivity to pain. This research underscores the intriguing link between gut health and joint management, suggesting that dietary strategies might positively affect physical capabilities beyond just the painful areas.

stories.title: Normal blood pressure may not tell the whole story: Scientists discover a brain ‘switch’
stories.summary: Hypertension impacts approximately 1.4 billion adults across the globe, with numerous individuals unaware of their status. A recent study by the University of Virginia uncovers essential brain cells responsible for maintaining stable blood pressure. These cells contribute to consistent blood pressure levels during daily activities and may mitigate abrupt changes.

stories.title: ‘IDBI bank was handed over to us in poor shape’: Sitharaman counters Rahul Gandhi
'20 markets, Rs 12,000cr trade at stake': Delhi traders urge Sonia Gandhi to defer Rahul Gandhi's November 1 rally
Court Orders Pipeline Review: Judge sends Summit CO2 route back to PSC; zoning and safety re‑examined
stories.summary: A North Dakota court ruling requires state regulators to reassess the Summit Carbon Solutions pipeline's approval process and local zoning ordinances. Emmons and Burleigh counties are challenging the state’s authority over pipeline routes, focusing on setback requirements. The Public Service Commission must now clarify its safety assessments and reconsider alternative routing options. Summit's broader carbon capture project faces multiple regulatory issues across several states, complicating its future.

US midterms: Trump skips rallies in red states, switches to phone campaign
Firecracker ban: No point in passing orders without enforcement, says SC
Taylor Swift gave $100,000 to a flood-hit Tennessee playground; now $3 million grant is sought
stories.summary: In 2010, Taylor Swift made a significant contribution of $100,000 to help rebuild the Kids Kingdom playground in Hendersonville after it was severely damaged by flooding. Originally built in 1996, the playground had encountered numerous safety challenges. Currently, officials are looking into a $3 million grant aimed at enhancing recreational facilities, particularly focusing on developing an all-inclusive playground for children of varying abilities.

Texas man Christophe Waggoner began October's Child in 2017; has gifted 8,000 Halloween costumes to families and plans to give away 4,000 in 2026
stories.summary: Christophe Waggoner established a charity called October's Child to provide Halloween costumes for children. He began the initiative after recalling his own childhood experiences with costumes. Over the years, the charity has grown significantly, distributing nearly 8,000 costumes to families in need. In the upcoming event, he plans to give away over 4,000 costumes for various age groups. Waggoner's efforts illustrate the positive impact of community support on childhood celebrations.

Bar bodies foiled plan to rope in ex-judges: Supreme Court
Mandate damages for savings lost in 'digital arrest': SC to RBI
CBI probes foreign funds to Arunachal activist
Inside Bieber Couple's Condo: Justin and Hailey add $12m West Village home; waterfront NYC base
stories.summary: Justin and Hailey Bieber have acquired a $12 million condominium in Manhattan's West Village. This residence features expansive river views and distinct architectural design. The apartment includes four bedrooms and significant amenities for privacy and convenience. The property reflects a modernist style and includes shared amenities like a swimming pool. This purchase adds to the couple's diverse real estate portfolio that spans multiple locations.

stories.title: Carney courts Europe as Trump’s trade war pushes Canada towards EU
After 20-Year Search, California Community Buys Cupertino Property for $16.5 Million
stories.summary: After an extensive search, the West Valley Muslim Association has successfully acquired a property in Cupertino for $16.5 million. This new facility will serve as a permanent home for the community, offering a venue for daily prayers, educational activities, and community gatherings. Supported by a dedicated fundraising campaign, this purchase reflects the growing needs of the local Muslim population, establishing a vital center for faith and fellowship.

stories.title: Mumbai gets its first nuclear science school at HSNC University
3,700-year-old man buried with stone in his mouth beneath a hearth may have been part of magical ritual
stories.summary: Approximately 3,700 years ago, a man in southeastern Spain underwent a burial unlike any other. Researchers suggest that this ritual may have been intended to symbolically overcome a threat rather than inflict punishment. The discovery of his body underneath a hearth, with a stone in his mouth, implies an effort to silence him.

stories.title: How UKHarvest turned food waste into 10 million meals
stories.summary: In 2017, Yvonne Thomson founded UKHarvest to address food waste and assist individuals facing food insecurity. Initially starting with one van, the charity has impressively salvaged 10 million meals throughout its journey. Its initiatives, including Community Food Hubs and Grub Clubs, offer not only affordable food but also valuable education. Collecting about 10 tonnes of excess food weekly, UKHarvest enjoys the patronage of Queen Camilla, amplifying its community impact.

stories.title: If you hire H-1B, you won't get grants: Texas Agriculture Department's new rule for businesses; 'Taxpayers work hard for their money'
Jammu & Kashmir HC strikes down water tax on hydropower projects
A helicopter with the EU force in Bosnia crashes, reportedly killing 3 and injuring 12
UT students wanted to condemn comments targeting Indian-origin students but university thought it was not just Bo French
Antipodes Island Sees Ground Beetle Numbers Surge 40-Fold After Mice Eradication
stories.summary: The successful removal of invasive house mice from Antipodes Island has spurred a remarkable resurgence in ground beetle populations, which have increased to around 40 times their former numbers. This ecological transformation highlights the beneficial effects of eradicating invasive species, fostering a healthier food web and aiding in the survival of native bird species. Long-term observation is crucial for comprehending the recovery dynamics of island ecosystems.

stories.title: Texas’s Historic Imperial Sugar Char House Gets $15M Rescue After 20 Years Vacant
stories.summary: Sugar Land City Council has given a green light for a $15 million initiative to safeguard the iconic Imperial Sugar Char House. This undertaking aims to stabilize the structure and prevent further deterioration over the years ahead. Work is set to commence shortly, with an anticipated completion by 2028. Officials are still finalizing plans for potential future utilizations, leaving residents eager for tangible development on this cherished landmark.

stories.title: SIR deadlines extended in 5 states, Delhi; EC sets new dates for final rolls
$410M plan to transform Connecticut power plant into waterfront park
Jamia sets date for student union poll, revokes disciplinary action against protesters
'Transgressions by China happen, it's not new': Arunachal CM says no intrusion along LAC
stories.summary: Pema Khandu asserted that border transgressions along the India-China frontier have been a longstanding issue, highlighting China's non-recognition of the McMahon Line. He described the recent confrontations as transgressions instead of intrusions and reassured citizens of the state's stability. Likewise, Union tourism minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat reaffirmed the safety of India's borders while working to alleviate media-induced tensions regarding the situation.

stories.title: Taking antibiotics? Eating a lot of sugar at the same time may make the damage to your gut worse, scientists have found, suggesting that what you eat during a course of antibiotics could affect how well your body recovers
stories.summary: Research findings indicate that a diet high in sugar can significantly affect the diversity of gut bacteria in patients undergoing antibiotic therapy. The study monitored the food intake and gut microbiome of hospitalized cancer patients treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, revealing a strong connection between elevated sugar levels and shifts in gut bacteria.

stories.title: In 1987, an amateur fossil hunter found a T. rex in South Dakota; the $31.8 million skeleton now stands in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: In 1987, Stan Sacrison found a T. rex skeleton in South Dakota, which was later sold for $31.8 million. Initially misidentified, the bones were correctly recognized as belonging to a T. rex in 1992. After years at the Black Hills Institute, the skeleton was auctioned and purchased for a museum in Abu Dhabi. Stan is now displayed in a dramatic scene depicting conflicts with another T. rex.

stories.title: 'Keeping a list of names': Abhishek Banerjee warns cops trying to 'please' Suvendu
Texas Jury Finds No Legal or Informal Adoption in $1 Million Inheritance Dispute
stories.summary: In a complex Texas inheritance case, a stepson referred to as 'my child' in a will navigated a treacherous dispute following his father's passing. Despite his claims of informal adoption, the family remained unconvinced. Ultimately, the jury affirmed that no formal or informal adoption occurred. This outcome highlights the necessity of clear legal documentation in estate planning to avoid misunderstandings, particularly within blended families concerning rights to inheritance.

stories.title: Steven Spielberg pulls $29.9 M LA ranch off the market
stories.summary: Filmmaker Steven Spielberg listed his Los Angeles ranch for $29.9 million but has now taken it off the market. He and his wife purchased the property in 1999 for $5.75 million, intending to create equestrian facilities. After facing opposition from local residents, their renovation plans were significantly reduced over the years. The ranch, known as Dogwood, features a main house with numerous upscale amenities and a 20,000-square-foot riding arena.

stories.title: In 1600, William Gilbert called Earth a giant magnet; his book sold for Rs 58.5 lakh in 2026
stories.summary: William Gilbert's pivotal publication, De Magnete, emerged in 1600, marking a significant shift in the exploration of magnetism and electricity. It introduced key terms and experimental approaches that influenced future electrical studies. The concept of Earth as a colossal magnet was groundbreaking. Recently, a first edition fetched $61,440 at a Christie’s auction, highlighting its enduring significance and the continued fascination it holds in scientific discourse.

stories.title: In 2022, conservators X-raying a Van Gogh painting in Edinburgh found a hidden self-portrait of the artist on the back of the canvas, concealed for more than a century under layers of glue and cardboard
stories.summary: A self-portrait of Vincent van Gogh was discovered concealed behind another painting after many years. The hidden portrait was found during routine examinations ahead of an exhibition. This discovery highlights Van Gogh's habit of reusing canvases due to financial difficulties throughout his life. Conservators are now working to reveal the portrait without damaging the original painting. Visitors to the exhibition were able to view the hidden portrait's X-ray image.

stories.title: Netanyahu's unity government gambit: Can he lure Eisenkot from opposition?
Trump official reacts to leaked video of Microsoft's AI chief telling staff company wants to bring foreign talents: 'You were hoping we were kidding'
Texas homeowners win control of their park, roads and ponds after a decade-long legal battle
stories.summary: In a significant turn of events, residents of La Bota Ranch in Laredo officially gained control over common property areas after a protracted legal battle. This shift follows a jury's March 2022 decision that found developers had breached fiduciary duties, prompting residents to reevaluate governance due to rising association fees. The final handover on August 20, 2026, empowers homeowners over shared facilities, symbolizing a hard-won victory for community representation.

stories.title: 'Don't push us': SC warns of harsh stand on firecrackers if orders go unenforced
stories.summary: The Supreme Court tackled the persistent air pollution crisis in Delhi-NCR, stressing the importance of adhering to current firecracker laws. Authorities were cautioned against inaction, as deteriorating air quality poses a threat to public health. The bench underlined the necessity for collaboration among all parties to effectively manage firecracker usage. Measures taken by the Delhi government include restrictions on older vehicles and staggered work hours.

stories.title: A 3,106-carat diamond pulled from a South African mine became the 530-carat gem in Britain's royal sceptre
stories.summary: Frederick Wells discovered the enormous Cullinan diamond in South Africa in 1905 while working at the Premier Mine. Its exceptional size caught public attention, leading to its purchase by the Transvaal government for King Edward VII. The diamond was carefully cut into several gemstones over eight months, resulting in noteworthy pieces for the British royal collection. Following Edward VII's death, the largest stone was incorporated into the Sovereign's Sceptre.

stories.title: An Indy charity started in 2016 with $9k raised in 45 mins; 10 yrs on, it reached 175k bouquets
stories.summary: Random Acts of Flowers Indianapolis marked ten years of service, delivering its 175,000th flower arrangement to Eskenazi Health. This charity reuses donated flowers to create arrangements for hospital patients in need. Volunteers collect flowers from various local sources to prevent waste and support emotional well-being. The organization was founded after a successful fundraising effort in 2016. It aims to continue its work through community partnerships and ongoing donations.

stories.title: Newly identified bird like dinosaur from Cretaceous period may be first dinosaur eating fruit
stories.summary: Scientists have recently uncovered a small dinosaur named Infernogallus jamesi, believed to have predominantly dined on fruit. By examining its skull and jaw muscles, researchers gained insights into its dietary habits. Existing during the Cretaceous period, as flowering plants flourished, this dinosaur displays anatomical traits akin to modern fruit-feeding parrots, deepening our comprehension of the varied lifestyles in the era of dinosaurs.

stories.title: 'Educated voters don't turn up in assembly polls': UP minister OP Rajbhar plays down MLC results
Royal regret! British king 'recognises' slavery horrors amid his Caribbean tour
stories.summary: Despite the pressure, Buckingham Palace has said Charles will not issue an apology during the tour, arguing that such matters are “matters for governments to address”. The palace added that he would “not shy away from the darkest days of our past.” As monarch, Charles represents Britain abroad on the advice of the government.

stories.title: The asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago may have also set the stage for ants to conquer the planet, with scientists finding a surprising boost from so-called jumping genes hidden in ant DNA
stories.summary: Since the dinosaurs vanished, ants have flourished, with more than 15,000 species recognized globally. New research, spearheaded by Dr. Lukas Schrader, highlights the role of jumping genes in their evolution and resilience. Significant surges of these genes occurred during the early Paleogene period, enhancing ants' olfactory receptors and social communication skills, thus providing a genetic edge for survival in diverse environments.

stories.title: Why do some people stay mentally sharp even when their brains show clear signs of Alzheimer’s disease? Scientists have found an important clue hidden in a rare group of resilient brains
stories.summary: Recent research from the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience has revealed intriguing findings about Alzheimer's disease. Scientists examined brain tissues from different groups, including those with and without dementia symptoms. They discovered that immature neurons acted differently in cognitively healthy individuals despite Alzheimer's brain changes. This suggests that these neurons may play a role in supporting brain function rather than simply replacing damaged cells.

stories.title: He wrote a book on 'Black Money', Feds tracked his $900K loan fraud: Indian-origin accountant jailed in Texas, investigator says 'I can only imagine his shock...'
University of Florida seeks an H-1B for a financial analyst, president Bell says it was made without his approval
MLC poll setback opens new front within Mahayuti; Shinde-for-CM pitch, 'Shakuni mama' jibe fly
'Double loss of double engine': Akhilesh mocks BJP over UP MLC poll results
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav criticized the BJP following their loss in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections held recently. He attributed the victory to teachers and young voters while alleging electoral manipulation by the BJP. The Samajwadi Party leader believes this defeat sets the foundation for the upcoming 2027 assembly elections. Yadav emphasized unity among marginalized communities and expressed gratitude towards supporters for their vigilance during the counting process.

stories.title: Mississippi father gives wife home promised to three children; daughter loses court battle
stories.summary: A Mississippi father left his family home and 0.86 acres of land equally to his three children in a 2008 will but transferred the property to his wife in 2021. After his death, his daughter challenged the transfer, claiming he had been improperly influenced due to his declining health. On Tuesday, an appeals court rejected her challenge, finding insufficient evidence of undue influence.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Pakistani lawmaker mocks Khawaja Asif after Munir’s Iran visit; SC wonders what's 'wrong' with victims of digital arrest & more
Wildlife traffickers may have killed her family to capture her; rescued baby gorilla Bili begins a second life in Congo
stories.summary: Bili, the young gorilla saved from wildlife trafficking in Nigeria, has embarked on a fresh journey in the Republic of the Congo. After three years of dedicated care and rehabilitation, she is now set for a quarantine period at the Tchimpounga Nature Reserve. Here, Bili will undergo health assessments and prepare for her introduction to fellow gorillas, with hopes of eventually reintegrating her into the wild.

stories.title: Minecraft creator lists Beverly Hills estate for $70M
stories.summary: Markus 'Notch' Persson has placed his Beverly Hills mansion on the market for $70 million. He purchased the estate in 2014 after outbidding Beyoncé and Jay-Z, who also showed interest. The mansion features eight bedrooms, a nightclub, and a professional recording studio for entertainment. The billionaire decided to sell as he spends less time in Los Angeles these days.

stories.summary: In Toms River, New Jersey, a family contested a neighbour's pool due to flooding fears. 13,800-year-old Alaska campsite reveals tools, a hearth and clues to early life near Beringia

Researchers identified activities such as food processing, toolmaking, and clothing production among early inhabitants. Comparisons with similar tools in Siberia suggest cultural connections across the Bering Land Bridge.

stories.summary: Cyclone Arnab is intensifying and is forecasted to hit the Andhra Pradesh coastline by Wednesday morning. The India Meteorological Department has issued alerts for severe winds and torrential rainfall affecting multiple states. Emergency shelters and control rooms are set up as beach access is prohibited to ensure public safety. Heavy rains are also impacting Odisha and Jharkhand. Residents are urged to stay updated and minimize travel during the cyclone's effects.

Nearly 30-year-old Magnum Ego ice cream found frozen in 145-year-old Australian store
stories.summary: During a recent freezer renovation in Harrow, Victoria, a shopkeeper stumbled upon a Magnum Ego ice cream believed to be nearly 30 years old. This finding, dating back to the late 1990s, has sparked a wave of nostalgia among Australians reminiscing about their childhood indulgences. Alongside this classic treat, other forgotten snacks like chips and milk containers were also uncovered.

Jon Bon Jovi's Toms River restaurant serves diners facing food insecurity; over 80% of meals went to guests in need in early 2026
stories.summary: In the first half of 2026, JBJ Soul Kitchen in Toms River played a crucial role in combating food insecurity, serving over 15,870 meals at a temporary pop-up. This unique restaurant model fosters a community atmosphere, inviting both paying diners and volunteers to partake in shared meals. Beyond nourishment, it connects individuals with vital resources for housing and mental health support.

stories.title: Texas grandfather wins $93,778 case against grandchildren's mother over unpaid child support
stories.summary: A Texas grandfather who gained custody of his three grandchildren after their father's death in 2017 has won a legal battle against their mother over unpaid child support and medical expenses. On October 23, a Texas appeals court upheld a $93,778 judgment against the mother, including $65,532 in medical costs. The mother had challenged the payments, arguing that the grandfather had not provided sufficient documentation to support his claims.

stories.title: Florida city opens $31 million botanical and wellness park at 209-acre Tucker Ranch preserve
stories.summary: On October 23, 2026, Tucker Ranch Holistic Health and Wellness Park along with its Botanical Garden opened its doors to the public. This remarkable transformation of a former cattle ranch spans 25.6 acres, featuring stunning botanical displays, outdoor fitness spaces, and wellness facilities initiated through a substantial investment. Its mission is to foster health, education, and outdoor engagement for both residents and visitors, with free daily access for all.

Centre to train 10,000 healthcare workers in drug de-addiction by 2029
stories.summary: India's health ministry has initiated a program to train 10,000 healthcare professionals on substance use disorders. The program aims to improve prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of addiction to substances like alcohol and opioids. In the current fiscal year, 2,000 personnel will be trained, with further increments planned over the next two years. Training will be provided through both online and offline methods across various healthcare institutions.

stories.summary: In an inspiring private fundraising gala, Ed Sheeran performed in New York, raising a remarkable $1 million to support disadvantaged children in Suffolk. Local charities will benefit from the funds, which Ipswich Town Football Club chairman Mark Ashton praised. The Lentonbrook Foundation plans to enhance its existing programs for youth in need, ensuring that the community continues to receive vital support.

stories.title: Wyoming landowner’s kitchenless guest house claim rejected by federal appeals court
stories.summary: Gary Binning confronted challenges while trying to build a guest house on his conservation-eased property, as a former Wyoming Supreme Court ruling placed restrictions on residential constructions. Despite his efforts to propose a design without a kitchen in talks with The Nature Conservancy, his idea was rejected due to its multiple residential characteristics. Ultimately, the courts dismissed the case, citing a lack of clarity and reasonable argument in Binning's claims.

stories.title: After 160 years of excavations, archaeologists find a 2,800-year-old bone flute at ancient Troy
stories.summary: For the first time in 160 years, archaeologists unearthed a bone flute at Troy, dating back approximately 2,800 years. In addition, they found a humanoid idol from the Early Bronze Age, offering new insights into the region's cultural traditions. The discoveries were announced by Turkish Minister of Culture and Tourism, Mehmet Nuri Ersoy. This time period correlates with the legendary works of Greek poet Homer.

stories.title: CDC deputy director Jennifer Shuford to exit role after midterms amid vaccine policy changes: Report
stories.summary: Jennifer Shuford, the chief medical officer of the CDC, plans to step down following the midterm elections due to shifts in the Trump administration's vaccine strategy. This new approach introduces a segmented vaccination regimen. Speculations about her exit suggest personal health concerns or differing views on vaccine messaging may have influenced her departure. The CDC and White House have yet to publicly address Shuford's upcoming exit.

Ocean Mixing Barrier Shown: Dye experiment maps slow downward transport; layered structure limits exchange
stories.summary: In a recent experiment near Martha’s Vineyard, scientists introduced rhodamine dye into the Atlantic Ocean to study its behavior. The dye spread quickly in the surface waters but demonstrated a slower descent into deeper layers. Findings showed a marked difference in mixing rates, emphasizing the complexities of ocean stratification on substance movement. This research is vital for the advancement of nutrient and pollutant transport models.

Shi asserts that the city violated state law’s requirements for prompt reviews. stories.summary: New Zealand's critically endangered southern dotterel population has risen by 52 percent following focused predator control efforts. Intensive campaigns targeting feral cats on Stewart Island have yielded immediate gains in breeding. The population grew from 105 birds in early 2025 to an estimated 160 in April 2026. Wildlife officials stress that ongoing management of feral cats is crucial for the bird's long-term survival.

California farmer triples walnut revenue by selling directly to 300 customers from a list of 10k
stories.summary: A walnut farmer in California revolutionized his sales with a targeted email marketing campaign. Reaching out to prior cherry customers, he uncovered 300 interested buyers for his walnuts. This approach resulted in his gross revenue tripling against wholesale prices, proving that even a small customer base can boost income stability. Consequently, many farmers are now embracing direct sales strategies to lessen financial uncertainties.

While the 45-room property remains empty, he survives on donated food and clothes, uses power banks to read books on his phone and relies on charity services for essentials. Neighbours have gradually accepted his presence.

stories.title: Man buys box of old medals for £25, discovers rare Captain Cook medal worth £5,000
stories.summary: A man who bought a box of 22 old medals for just £25 at a car-boot sale in West Yorkshire discovered that one was a rare 18th-century medal commemorating Captain James Cook's death in 1779. After selling the other medals for £500, he took the rare piece to an auction house, where it later fetched £5,000. The medal was purchased by the Captain Cook Memorial Museum in Whitby for a special exhibition planned for 2028.

stories.summary: Tyler Perry has listed his Beverly Hills mansion for $57 million amid plans to relocate to Puerto Rico. The estate, known for hosting Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, spans approximately 24,600 square feet. Featuring eight bedrooms and extensive amenities, it offers privacy within the exclusive Beverly Ridge Estates community. Oka placed strong emphasis on civil discourse as a pillar of democracy and raised alarms about environmental issues fueling rising temperatures in urban areas like Thane and Mumbai. The Michigan Court of Appeals reversed an earlier court decision and ordered the protection order to be canceled. This dispute arose after the mother moved to Michigan with their child, preventing scheduled parenting time. The appeals court found that the mother did not provide sufficient evidence for the protection order.

stories.summary: A Michigan appeals court has made headlines by overturning a hefty judgment against a couple who backed out of purchasing a luxury residence. stories.summary: Vanessa Trump has revealed that extreme fatigue was the first sign of her “very invasive” breast cancer, diagnosed six months ago. Now cancer-free after undergoing a lumpectomy and radiation treatment, she has shared details of her recovery and encouraged people to prioritise their health, schedule regular screenings and understand the importance of early detection.

stories.summary: The US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit has made a pivotal ruling concerning immigrant detention, involving three men who unlawfully entered the country. The court decided to overturn earlier decisions that allowed them individualized bond hearings while awaiting removal proceedings. This change stirs substantial dialogue on the potential impacts on the constitutional rights of immigrants facing detention without due process.

stories.title: A 400-year-old Mughal carpet owned by a US financier, novelist and the Thyssen family returns to auction
stories.summary: A remarkable relic from the Mughal era, the 'Yerkes-Remarque' carpet, is set to go under the hammer at Sotheby's. CS Setty, SBI chairman, underscored that bolstering cybersecurity is crucial for maintaining customer trust and proactively addressing threats, alongside regular training for employees and raising customer awareness on digital safety.

stories.title: 25 Arizona voters wrongly flagged by Trump administration regain voting rights days before midterms
stories.summary: Twenty-five US citizens in Arizona have regained their voting access after being wrongly flagged as possible noncitizens. stories.title: At 17, British student Max Budgen drew 1,300 flipbook pages to set a Guinness World Record
stories.summary: Max Budgen, a 17-year-old student from Petersfield, Hampshire, created a 1,300-page hand-drawn flipbook. He devoted over three weeks to complete this ambitious project while facing challenges. Max experienced boredom and a lack of ideas at times but remained determined to continue. Reaching significant milestones, such as 300 and 1,000 pages, motivated him throughout the process.

stories.title: Irish father loses wedding ring in Italian stream; 3 strangers fly to Ireland to return it
stories.summary: During a delightful family vacation in Italy, an Irish father accidentally lost his wedding ring while enjoying time with his kids. Determined to recover it, his wife enlisted the help of three local good Samaritans who tirelessly searched the river for three days. The Kenai Peninsula Borough Planning Commission initially rejected the permit due to significant environmental impact concerns. After several appeals and court rulings, the Alaska Supreme Court upheld the commission's decision in October 2026. The court found substantial evidence showed potential noise and visual disturbances could not be minimized.

Trump’s Kennedy Center row deepens as lawmaker demands nearly 200 secret text messages

The request comes amid a legal dispute over plans to close the performing arts centre for renovations, months after a judge ruled that Trump's name had been illegally added to the building and ordered its removal.

stories.title: 'Unforgivable': MP minister Vishvas Sarang slams Kharge over remark on PM Modi
stories.summary: In a recent event marking Dr. Krishna Singh's birth anniversary in Patna, Madhya Pradesh minister Vishvas Sarang took aim at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for his disparaging remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's late parents. Sarang criticized the need for greater respect towards cultural customs surrounding the deceased, labeling Kharge's comments as wholly unacceptable. He condemned the Congress party's silence on the matter, voicing concern over their current political behavior.

stories.title: 'We hear you': Rahul Gandhi's message to traders in Delhi amid anti-CEC stir
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has publicly backed the traders in Delhi struggling from the ramifications of ongoing protests and governmental restrictions. He pointed fingers at the administration for hampering commerce by suspending metro services and blocking roads. Traders are reportedly facing losses of around Rs 3,000 crore following previous rallies in October.

stories.title: Zendaya expands Hollywood Hills estate with another $2M home
stories.summary: Zendaya began her real estate journey with a Mediterranean-style home purchased at age 20 in San Fernando Valley. She later acquired a ranch-style estate in Encino and a luxury condo in Brooklyn Heights. Recently, Zendaya bought a mid-century modern home in Hollywood Hills, previously owned by Ashley Tisdale. She subsequently purchased a neighboring property, a fixer-upper, signaling her intent to renovate it.

stories.title: Australia expands biometric requirements for visa applicants in India from October 26
Edinburgh rejects 212MW data centre as Scottish Ministers review appeal
'Insult to India itself': Rajnath Singh attacks Kharge over 'baap' remark against PM Modi
stories.summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh has taken a strong stand against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's statements about Prime Minister Modi, labeling them as disrespectful to both the leader and the nation. Singh asserted that Modi remains focused on serving citizens and undeterred by such comments. Following these remarks, a protest by the BJP's Patna Metropolitan unit was promptly organized.

Rahul Gandhi acquitted in 2018 defamation case over remarks on Amit Shah
stories.summary: A special MP/MLA court in Sultanpur dismissed a defamation case against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on Monday. This case originated in 2018 due to remarks Gandhi made about Amit Shah during a rally. Vijay Mishra, a local BJP politician, filed the complaint alleging Gandhi's comments were defamatory. Rahul Gandhi appeared before the court in 2023, where he secured bail successfully.

stories.title: AI model uses face photos to estimate biological age, predict survival risk in cancer patients
stories.summary: A new AI model, FAHR-Face, estimates biological age and predicts cancer patient survival risk using facial photos. This model was trained on millions of images and showed an average error of about five years. Alongside this, another model identified high-risk cancer patients based on their appearance, highlighting significant survival differences. While results were promising in the US and Netherlands, further validation is needed in other populations.

PM Modi congratulates Brazil's Lula on re-election, says will advance Global South cooperation

Trump Claims Trade Imbalance: accuses Canada of exploiting US; says deal likely but no rush
stories.summary: Donald Trump has voiced concerns that Canada has been exploiting trade advantages over the United States for years. He asserts that talks between the nations are nearing a satisfactory agreement for the U.S. economy. Trump advocates for a sustainable deal rather than a temporary fix, criticizing Canadian tariffs and calling for transparency in trade practices. Despite the friction, he remains hopeful for a resolution to the ongoing trade conflict.

stories.title: ABBA’s Chiquitita raised over $5 million for UNICEF in 45 years; how the 1979 hit continues to protect children
stories.summary: ABBA's song Chiquitita has raised over US$5 million for UNICEF since its release in 1979. This funding supports various programs aimed at protecting vulnerable children from abuse and violence. The pledge originated during a concert at the United Nations to promote children's rights. In 2021, ABBA extended its support by pledging royalties from another song to UNICEF.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia’s Singapore plan: How Riyadh aims to protect Asian oil supplies from 2027
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is set to store crude oil in Singapore starting in the second half of 2027. This arrangement aims to enhance energy security in the region amid supply disruptions. Singapore's Jurong Rock Caverns will provide storage facilities for Saudi crude oil supplies. The agreement will allow Saudi Aramco to bring supplies closer to key Asian markets.

stories.title: BJP files police complaint against Kharge over 'baap' remark targeting PM Modi
stories.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party has lodged a police complaint against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge in Patna. The complaint relates to Kharge's remarks about Prime Minister Modi during an event during 139th birth anniversary Bihar's first CM, Shrikrishna Singh. Krishna Kumar Singh, a BJP worker, demands an apology from Kharge within 24 hours. The initial report was filed at Kotwali police station, then transferred to Gandhi Maidan.

'Utilizing Iran for politics': IDF chief, Netanyahu clash over military action ahead of Israel elections - report
stories.summary: Tension brews within Israel's leadership as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and IDF chief Eyal Zamir disagree on possible military action against Iran. This clash before elections raises eyebrows about political motives behind military strategies. Netanyahu highlights the imminent threat Iran poses and urges immediate action during Trump's administration. As the election approaches, Netanyahu faces tight competition from Gadi Eisenkot, suggesting possible political deadlock with no clear majority in view.

stories.title: 'Had enough': Thousands protest in Prague against Czech government's public media funding overhaul
stories.summary: Thousands gathered in Prague to protest government proposals affecting public television and radio funding. The planned changes would replace licence fees with state budget allocations, raising concerns about media independence. Critics argue that these measures may expose broadcasters to political pressure and reduce their financial stability. Public media employees announced plans for a strike on November 3, with a larger rally scheduled for November 15.

‘Vote for Netanyahu’: Trump urges Israelis to re-elect ‘outstanding warrior’ PM
stories.summary: HHNBAhead of the crucial Israeli elections, Donald Trump has thrown his support behind Benjamin Netanyahu, underlining the critical role their alliance plays in countering Iran's threats to both nations. Trump praised Netanyahu's effectiveness as a leader throughout their joint military efforts, despite previous tensions regarding their strategies towards Iran. This endorsement marks a notable moment as it's uncommon for a sitting U.S.

stories.title: Riyadh airport partially reopens: Saudi intercepts Houthi ballistic missile, drones
stories.summary: A Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, claiming to protect the capital. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree described King Khalid International Airport as unsafe for travellers and staff. The airport administration designated terminals for domestic and international flights despite warnings. Additionally, attacks against Yemeni civilian sites by Saudi warplanes were claimed to be extensive. Claims made by both sides regarding missile interceptions and airstrikes remain unverified.

Massive fire engulfs Shiv Market near Jammu Railway Station, 35-40 shops gutted
John Stamos’ former California mansion drops from $13 million to $6.4 million after renovations
stories.summary: John Stamos’s luxurious California mansion has experienced substantial price drops since 2025. Initially, this Mediterranean-style estate in Calabasas was priced near $13 million, but after renovations by the current owners, it now stands at about $6.4 million. Stamos originally acquired the property in 1991 for $430,000 and sold it in 2001, illustrating the complexities in marketing highly personalized high-end real estate.

stories.title: Philadelphia Orchestra marks 14th China tour with $10.5m gift for global tours and new music
stories.summary: David L Cohen and Rhonda R Cohen have made an impressive commitment of $10.5 million to the Philadelphia Orchestra. This significant donation aims to fund international tours and foster cultural exchanges, while also introducing new music initiatives worldwide. Their contribution will establish the Fund for Cultural Diplomacy, enhancing the orchestra's role as a cultural ambassador, alongside launching the Artistic Innovation and Discovery Fund to spotlight underrepresented composers.

EC refuses to give details of SIR software, cites ‘trade secrets, IPR'
stories.summary: Election Commission of India declined to share the name of the software used for identifying electoral roll errors. The request for information was made under the Right to Information Act. A social activist from Telangana sought details about the software and algorithms used in the process. The Commission stated that no new software was developed for the exercise conducted.

stories.title: Hendrie Ranch Conservation Easement: Florida approves $12.9m deal; wildlife corridor stays working
stories.summary: A 5,610-acre section of Hendrie Ranch will remain undeveloped due to a $12.9 million conservation easement. This agreement, approved by state officials, allows continued agricultural use while protecting the land from development. The ranch supports cattle, hay production, and timber harvesting alongside diverse wildlife habitats. It is part of Florida's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program to safeguard agricultural properties.

stories.title: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to government than needed, says Justice Kaul
stories.summary: Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has expressed concerns about how former Chief Justice D Y Chandrachud dealt with the government. He believes Chandrachud was too lenient during the process of judicial appointments, which raises worries about the independence of the judiciary. This could potentially undermine the separation between the courts and the government, according to Kaul.

stories.title: EPFO considers Rs 25,000cr war chest to stabilise interest payouts
stories.summary: Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation is exploring the establishment of a Rs 25,000-crore Interest Stabilisation Reserve. This reserve aims to protect members’ interest payouts from corporate bond defaults and other market fluctuations. A report suggested that the fund should be built via surplus ETF gains and will invest in government securities. Historical performance indicates that this reserve can effectively manage interest rate stability.

stories.title: Delaware couple wins HOA garage dispute as court orders removal of property violation notice
stories.summary: John and Sandra Mitchell have won a court case against their homeowners association regarding garage construction plans. They proposed a 24-by-28-foot garage with metal siding, which the board initially rejected. The court ruled that the association overstepped its authority by denying the materials without clear restrictions. The violation notice against their property was ordered to be removed from public records.

stories.title: BJP calls protest over Kharge’s ‘baap’ remark
stories.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's comment about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's father sparked widespread outrage among BJP members. Following the incident, the BJP announced nationwide protests against Kharge's remarks, labeling them indecent and offensive. Union home minister Amit Shah criticized Congress for personal attacks and blamed it on their electoral disappointments. Kharge also condemned the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, describing it as a threat to democracy.

stories.title: New York man challenges bank over 2005 mortgage, wins appeal in foreclosure dispute
stories.summary: A New York homeowner who took out a mortgage in 2005 has secured a reversal of a foreclosure ruling that had favoured US Bank National Association. Moses Sukljian challenged the bank's right to enforce the loan after it accused him of missing payments. On Friday, an appeals court overturned the earlier ruling, finding that the bank had failed to provide sufficient proof of its legal standing.

stories.title: Trump gears up for Iran escalation after US polls; Tehran says position unchanged
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has signaled potential military action against Iran following the upcoming midterm elections. The US has increased its military presence in the Persian Gulf with additional aircraft and troops. Iran is reportedly preparing for retaliation against US and allied interests in the region. Both Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu may view renewed conflict as a political strategy.

stories.title: Kentucky court halts inquiry into widow's mental capacity after she rejects late husband's will
stories.summary: A Kentucky appeals court ruled that a district court could not investigate Tamara Williams' mental capacity claim. The dispute arose over her choice to reject her late husband Julian D. Williams' will for a statutory share. After her husband's death, Tamara's decision was contested by his stepchildren, who claimed she lacked mental capacity. The appeals court determined that contested cases must be resolved in circuit court rather than district court.

George Harrison donated his album royalties to charity. In 2024, his foundation spent £573,221
stories.summary: George Harrison's Material World Foundation continues to thrive, providing substantial funding to charitable initiatives worldwide. In 2024 alone, the foundation allocated over £573,000 towards public health, education, and emergency relief efforts. Operated independently by a board of trustees including Olivia Harrison, it eschews salaries to focus all resources on its mission. Founded from royalties of Harrison's classic album, Living in the Material World, the foundation's influence endures, promoting lasting change.

stories.title: New York couple pledges $10 million to expand NICU after granddaughter’s birth experience
stories.summary: Donald and Barbara Zucker have pledged a remarkable $10 million to elevate the standard of neonatal intensive care at Good Samaritan University Hospital. This generous commitment will be complemented by donations from the community, amplifying its reach. The initiative aims to upgrade the neonatal unit with cutting-edge technology and supportive amenities, ensuring high-risk newborns and their families receive essential care in a nurturing environment close to home.

stories.title: Kansas appeals court reopens divorce property case after jailed husband missed hearing next door
stories.summary: A Kansas appeals court recently vacated a previous ruling in a divorce property case, asserting that Scott L. Hale was not given a fair chance to participate. Haltingly unable to attend his hearing due to incarceration, Scott's objections to the property division were overlooked by the trial judge. The court's decision sends the matter back to the lower court for a comprehensive reassessment and new hearing.

stories.title: Give mayors real powers, ensure timely civic audits, urban body heads tell Centre
Texas student builds landscaping business to fund college, wins national agribusiness award
stories.summary: Texas student Jose Yepez started a landscaping business to pay for college, but it soon grew into a company serving more than 100 clients and employing four full-time workers. The business has also helped him support his family financially. His efforts earned him the 2026 American Star in Agribusiness award from the National FFA Organization on Friday.

stories.title: 80-ton boulder collapses at park after 104 years, smashing a walkway but injuring no one
stories.summary: In a surprising turn of events on October 18, 2026, an 80-ton granite boulder collapsed at Polar Caves Park in Rumney, New Hampshire, smashing a wooden walkway and its safety rails. Fortunately, this incident resulted in no injuries. The boulder's fall is likely due to weather-related erosion. Park authorities are now assessing the situation and implementing repair plans to allow for a safe return of visitors in spring 2027.

stories.title: Alabama lawyer gave up career to care for parents, but court upheld cancellation of her condo deed
stories.summary: The Alabama Supreme Court has affirmed a lower court's ruling that invalidated a property transfer from parents to their daughter, Holly Schumpert. Despite her dedication in caring for her ailing parents, the court determined the coastal condominium was part of a family trust, rendering the deed null. As a result, laws designed to protect elderly property owners allowed the reversal, leading to Holly having no claim to the estate.

stories.title: Delhi Police file FIR against opposition MPs over alleged trespassing at Jamia during student protest
stories.summary: The Delhi Police has launched an FIR targeting Congress MPs who attended the student protests at Jamia Millia Islamia. The MPs are accused of entering the university without permission amid ongoing demands for reinstating the students' union. Protesters are also calling for a halt to disciplinary measures against students and improved campus facilities, while university officials draft guidelines for upcoming union elections, adding to the complexity of the situation.

Trump says he needs to 'stop killing Iranian leaders' to find someone to negotiate with
DNA evidence solves 2012 murder of North Carolina student Faith Hedgepeth, 14 years later
stories.summary: Miguel Salguero Olivares has received a life sentence for the chilling murder of Faith Hedgepeth, whose case remained a mystery for nearly ten years. Thanks to DNA evidence, he was arrested and convicted of first-degree murder, rape, and burglary. Faith's lifeless body was found in her apartment in September 2012 after a fun night out.

stories.title: After years of abandonment, 48 acres once home to Ohio's SeaWorld and Six Flags parks are set to reopen on October 25
stories.summary: Aurora Park at Geauga Lake will reopen to the public on October 25, focusing on outdoor recreation. This redevelopment includes seating areas, boating access, and restored structures from the amusement park era. Future phases will introduce a public beach, playground, and other recreational facilities as part of the project. The City of Aurora acquired the property in December 2024 to ensure public access.

stories.title: Arctic ice had been expanding for 1,000 years before reaching its greatest extent around 1960
stories.summary: A recent study indicates that the Barnes Ice Cap had begun expanding nearly 2,000 years ago. This expansion was attributed to cooler summer conditions that allowed ice to grow. However, rising greenhouse gas emissions reversed this trend and caused significant ice retreat since the 1960s. Researchers emphasize that human-induced warming has disrupted natural climate patterns that favored renewed glacial growth.

stories.title: Pope Leo urges end to Yemen violence after lung cancer surgery
Lost Joan Eardley painting found in charity shop after 64 years, selling for £29,500 for research
stories.summary: In an unexpected twist, a stunning landscape painting by Scottish talent Joan Eardley was discovered in an English charity shop. Named Summer Fields, the artwork fetched an impressive £29,500, with proceeds dedicated to funding medical research. After a paper label revealed its authenticity, the piece was returned to Scotland for further evaluation. This sale highlights the increasing appreciation for Eardley’s influence on mid-20th century art, celebrated in various exhibitions.

About 1,300 abuse survivors agree to an $800m NY Catholic Church settlement, pending signatures
stories.summary: The Catholic Archdiocese of New York has reached an $800 million settlement for around 1,300 survivors of sexual abuse. This settlement resulted from lawsuits filed under the Child Victims Act, which allowed claims despite prior time limits. Payments will be determined through an independent review process based on the severity of the abuse and its impact. The archdiocese plans to improve transparency by releasing more records related to accused clergy.

stories.title: Built in 1834, a 75,000-pound Métis home crossed Georgian Bay after its owner sold it for $2
stories.summary: The historic Labatte House, a Métis residence from 1834, is set to be carefully moved to Balm Beach to ensure its preservation. Weighing approximately 75,000 pounds, the relocation is a meticulous endeavor across Georgian Bay. This effort seeks to create a museum dedicated to Indigenous and Métis narratives in the area, with restoration scheduled to start soon and a concrete foundation expected by spring 2027.

stories.title: After surviving cardiac arrest in 2023, Damar Hamlin helped 1,293 people learn CPR in one hour
stories.summary: Damar Hamlin set a Guinness World Record by successfully teaching hands-only CPR to 1,293 individuals at Acrisure Stadium. This event, part of a broader initiative in partnership with the American Heart Association, aimed to raise awareness about cardiac emergencies and emphasize the importance of immediate response. Fueled by his personal experience with cardiac arrest, Hamlin sought to empower his community with life-saving skills for potential emergencies.

stories.title: Crystal Drinkwalter & Jazmyn Canning built a $52K natural pond on their 65-acre land, saving $148K
stories.summary: On their sprawling 65-acre property, Crystal Drinkwalter and Jazmyn Canning took on the ambitious project of building a natural swimming pond after being deterred by high contractor fees. Through hard work, they relocated more than 100,000 pounds of rock and lined the pond by hand. It took eight water trucks to fill their 110,000-gallon pond with water. For a detailed look at this impressive feat, visit their YouTube channel.

stories.title: Mallikarjun Kharge’s 'baap' remark on PM Modi sparks row, BJP hits back
Trump's 250-foot arch could see construction begin November 5 despite pending legal challenge
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump's proposed 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington could begin construction as early as November 5, pending final approvals. However, three military veterans and a retired architectural historian have asked a federal judge to stop the work, arguing that congressional authorisation is required. The project faces two lawsuits questioning its approval process and legality.

Israel elections: Can Netanyahu turn security gains into a political victory?
stories.summary: Israeli voters will head to the polls on October 27 in a significant election for Benjamin Netanyahu. His political future hinges on addressing security failures following the October 7 attack by Hamas. Gadi Eisenkot has emerged as a primary challenger, emphasizing military accountability over Netanyahu's leadership. The election highlights divisions within the opposition and potential coalition challenges.

stories.title: Indian American physician Navin Shah commits $525,000 to infectious disease program in Pune
stories.summary: Dr. Navin C. Shah has committed $525,000 to establish a new infectious disease program at BJ Government Medical College. The initiative aims to enhance research, medical training, and patient care for underserved communities in Pune. Collaborating with Johns Hopkins University, the program will focus on public health challenges like tuberculosis and HIV. Faculty and student exchanges are also planned to foster international cooperation in medicine.

stories.title: ‘Don’t encourage Jinnah worship’: Keralam BJP chief Chandrashekhar targets CM Satheesan amid Fort Kochi video row
BSF apprehends four Pakistani fishermen in Kutch, seizes boat
stories.summary: On Sunday, four Pakistani fishermen were intercepted by the Border Security Force in the Kutch district of Gujarat. Suspected of illegally fishing in Indian waters for crabs, they were detained following precise intelligence alerts. The crew members, hailing from Chach Jaan Khan village in Sindh province, are now under investigation as the BSF maintains vigilance over the sensitive border region to thwart unauthorized entries.

stories.title: 24-year-old Coast Guard swimmer rescues 16 people from Pacific shipwreck after two hours in darkness
stories.summary: A US Coast Guard rescue swimmer undertook a challenging operation to save 16 individuals from the Pacific Ocean. The rescue followed a distress call regarding a capsized boat off Mexico's Baja California. Over 2,441 square miles were searched, but 11 victims remain missing as the search was suspended. Investigation into the vessel's circumstances is ongoing, and survivors received medical care before being processed under US immigration law.

'Second war of independence': Kharge targets BJP-RSS, calls for nationwide movement against SIR
No need to take blood pressure pills now? Scientists are testing a device that can reduce BP by stimulating nerves
stories.summary: A recent study shows that stimulating the ear can help lower blood pressure. Known as transcutaneous autonomic neuromodulation, this innovative approach may offer an effective solution for managing hypertension. In a clinical trial with 63 participants who struggled with uncontrolled hypertension despite medication, those with severe cases displayed encouraging results. However, further research is essential to validate the efficacy of this non-invasive technique.

stories.title: DK Shivakumar's big warning to Bengaluru IT firms over sidelining Kannadiga candidates
A former army chief, 2 ex-PMs and an Arab party leader: Netanyahu’s main rivals in Israel polls
In the 1940s, Ohio built a 200-foot dam for a village; now, it’s restoring a 14-mile creek
stories.summary: Ohio's Cloverlick Dam, built in the 1940s, is being removed to restore the natural flow of Cloverlick Creek. This restoration project aims to improve water quality and reconnect aquatic habitats that have been disrupted for decades. Removal of the dam is expected to create a safer environment for recreational activities like fishing and kayaking. Funding for the project is being provided by the H2Ohio Rivers Program and federal grants.

stories.title: Kentucky couple transferred $210,000 land for $1; appeals court upholds sale over $177,668 debt
stories.summary: A property transfer for just $1 has failed to shield a Kentucky couple’s land from a creditor seeking to recover an unpaid debt. In an October 23, 2026, opinion, the Kentucky Court of Appeals upheld an order allowing property assessed at approximately $210,000 to be sold to satisfy a judgment of $177,667.88, plus applicable costs and attorney fees.

stories.title: Natalie Portman's €15.2 million Paris mansion near the Eiffel Tower has a 100-year-old history
stories.summary: Natalie Portman purchased a 550-square-metre mansion in Paris for €15.2 million in September 2023. Built in 1912, the four-storey property once served as an embassy before undergoing extensive renovation. Located near the Eiffel Tower, the residence features a garden, gym, library, wine cellar and a glass-roofed reception room. The actress bought the property months before her divorce from Benjamin Millepied was finalised.

stories.title: Robert Kraft’s anti-hate group raises $32m at gala with Tom Brady, Jon Bon Jovi and 800 guests
stories.summary: More than 800 guests gathered at New York’s Waldorf Astoria on October 21, 2026, for an evening that combined celebrity appearances, philanthropy and a campaign against antisemitism and discrimination. The inaugural benefit gala of the Blue Square Alliance Against Hate, founded by New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, raised more than $32 million.

stories.title: J. M. Barrie and Keith Emerson’s former Sussex home lists for £3.75 million
ECINET row: Congress questions EC after poll body refuses to share details of ‘controversial’ software
'Don't film missiles': India advises its nationals in Saudi Arabia amid ongoing Houthi strikes
A festival, a DJ and a complaint: What residents can legally do about noise
David Gilmour’s Former Essex farmhouse listed for £1.1 million
